Client work fills the day. New inquiries still need a next step.

The situation

A small consultancy’s owner often handles sales alongside delivery. Replies, scheduling, and follow-ups compete with the work already promised to clients.

The existing options

Scheduling tools, client-management suites, and AI assistants already cover parts of this workflow. Relay needs to earn its place through a focused experience for small teams.

What we’re testing

Can one simple inquiry-to-follow-up workflow help an owner keep conversations moving with less manual effort? That’s the question this prototype is designed to explore.

HOW IT WORKS

Three steps, one hard rule.

1

It reads

Every inbound message is parsed for budget, timeline, service line and intent — then checked against the minimum project size you set.

2

It drafts

A reply in your tone that names their goal, handles the budget question honestly, asks your qualifying questions, and offers two times you actually have free.

3

You approve

Nothing sends on its own. The draft waits in your queue, you edit a line if you want, and you press send.

The hard rule: a client's email is data, never an instruction. Relay reads what they wrote; it never does what a message tells it to do. That's what makes an approval gate worth having.
THE FIRST CUSTOMER

Start with small U.S. consultancies and specialist agencies.

Who we want to help

Teams of two to ten people where the owner still handles incoming inquiries and new-business conversations. This is our proposed starting segment.

What we need to validate

How much time the workflow saves, whether it helps qualified prospects reach a meeting, and what owners will pay. Customer interviews and paid pilots come next.

Where it could grow

After validating the core workflow, explore deeper proposal follow-ups, onboarding, and client re-engagement. Expansion should follow customer needs.

HONEST STATUS

What works today, and what's next.

Working in the prototype

  • Inbound message parsing — budget, timeline, service, intent, fit
  • Draft generation in three configurable tones
  • Sample-calendar availability and conflict-checked booking
  • Calendar file (.ics) export and mail-client handoff
  • Pipeline stages, analytics and follow-up queue
  • An illustrative business-case calculator with editable inputs

Next build steps

  • Model-backed drafting behind the same approval gate
  • Gmail and Outlook OAuth for real inbound and sending
  • Google / Microsoft calendar sync
  • Accounts, workspaces and billing
  • Background follow-up scheduling

Plain about the boundaries: the drafting engine in this prototype is deterministic rules running in your browser, not a live model. Client data is fictional. Nothing is emailed, no calendar is connected, and changes save only to your own browser. A production version will also need secure account connections, reliable background processing, and tested model behavior behind the approval controls.
